memory_candidates.content: Engine-run predicate over-quantification is a recurring, refutable defect shape in MintBound.lean: every argument of an engine entry point (expandBranchWithFuel, saturateBlocked) that the CONSUMING site instantiates at a default is an over-quantification surface, and narrowing one such argument does not clear the others. Three instances now: fuel (C9 entry 22), the output branch (entry 23), and the EventualityTracker argument (task 463). The cheap refutation technique: build a witness the entry point returns at its FIRST step, so `rw [entryPoint]` unfolds the equation lemma exactly once and the `.saturated` arm closes the goal by rfl. This makes a kernel refutation cheap precisely where a kernel PROOF about the same well-founded-recursive function is prohibitive (which is why such predicates get probed with #guard_msgs measurements instead). Planning checklist for any such predicate: for each binder, ask whether the consuming site instantiates it at a default; if yes, that binder is a refutation lever.
